name: TX-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Fletcher's massive fundraising advantage ($1.7M on hand vs. $6K)
Incumbency and no serious outside spending against her
Prediction markets price Fletcher near-certain to win
model.rationale: Fletcher holds a D+13 seat with a huge cash advantage over an underfunded challenger, and markets price her at roughly 96% to win. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the fundamentals point to a comfortable incumbent win.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unusually strong national GOP environment could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains a long shot.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lizzie Fletcher seeks a fourth term in a Houston-area district that has shifted firmly Democratic since her 2018 upset, now carrying a D+13 partisan lean. She faces Republican Alexander Hale, a first-time challenger with minimal resources, plus a Green Party candidate on the ballot.

The financial picture is lopsided: Fletcher has raised $1.4 million and holds $1.7 million on hand, while Hale has raised under $80,000 with little cash remaining. No outside groups have invested in the race, no public polls have been conducted, and prediction markets give Fletcher roughly a 96% chance of winning. All signs point to a safe Democratic hold, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
